Druid.intro: The Druid is a shapeshifter: a caster and healer, a tough bear and a fast cat. You level in cat form for damage and switch to bear when several mobs attack. Between fights you shift back and heal yourself, so you almost never need to eat. Many buttons, but very forgiving once you learn them.
good: Heals yourself, so you rarely die
Bear, cat or caster: tank, damage or heal
Travel and Aquatic Form save lots of time
Can play every role in a group
bad: Many forms and buttons to learn
Shifting out to heal costs mana and time

levels.title: Nature magic first
tips: Keep Mark of the Wild and Thorns on yourself before every pull.
Pull with Wrath and keep Moonfire on the mob. Hit it with your staff when mana is low.
Heal with Rejuvenation after a fight instead of eating.
At level 10, visit your trainer for the Bear Form quest.

levels.title: Bear Form
tips: Pull with Moonfire, then shift to Bear Form. Furor gives you rage at once.
Demoralizing Roar makes mobs hit softer. Swipe hits several mobs at once.
After the fight, shift out, heal with Regrowth and drink only if mana is low.
Do the Aquatic Form quest at 16. Swimming is much faster.

levels.title: Cat Form for damage
tips: Cat Form at 20 is your main leveling form. Bear is for two or more mobs.
Build combo points with Claw, then spend them on Rip.
Open from Prowl with Rake to start a bleed right away.
Feral Swiftness makes your cat faster between mobs.

levels.title: Bleeds and speed
tips: Travel Form at 30 makes running between mobs much faster.
Rend and Tear gives more damage on bleeding mobs. Always Rake first.
Ferocious Bite is a strong finisher once the mob is almost dead.
Leader of the Pack helps any group you join.

levels.title: Dire Bear and Shifting Power
tips: Dire Bear Form at 40 makes you much tougher. Use it for groups of mobs.
Shifting Power turns your unused mana into energy. Use it when energy runs out.
Naturalist adds 10% to all your damage.
Barkskin at 44 cuts damage if a pull goes wrong.

levels.title: Strong and steady
tips: Thick Hide gives more armor in both forms.
Look for gear with Agility and Strength. Weapon damage does not matter in forms.
Try tanking a dungeon in Dire Bear Form. Groups always need a tank.

notes.8: Entangling Roots holds a mob while you cast or run.
notes.10: Bear Form quest and your first talent point.
notes.14: Bash stuns a mob. Great for stopping spells.
notes.30: Travel Form and Leader of the Pack.
notes.36: Frenzied Regeneration heals you in bear. Pounce from Prowl.
notes.41: Shifting Power talent: mana into energy.

end.title: Restoration for healing
end.text: At 60, Restoration makes you a strong healer with Swiftmend, Nature's Swiftness and Wild Growth. Groups and raids always look for healers.

Hunter.intro: A ranged fighter with a loyal pet. From level 10 your beast holds the mob while you shoot it down from a distance. Few classes level as smoothly: little resting, fast kills and Feign Death when things go wrong. You just need to keep ammo, pet food and some bag space.
good: Your pet tanks while you shoot
Fast kills with very little resting
Feign Death saves most bad pulls
bad: Needs ammo, pet food and bag space
Weak when a mob reaches melee range

levels.title: Shoot first
tips: Open with Serpent Sting, add Arcane Shot (6), and let Auto Shot do the rest.
Buy plenty of ammo and a quiver or ammo pouch. Running out means melee only.
If a mob reaches you, use Raptor Strike, then step back and keep shooting.

levels.title: Your first pet
tips: At 10 your class trainer gives the quests that unlock taming. Tame a beast at your level.
Send the pet in first and let it build threat for a second or two, then start shooting.
Feed your pet often. A happy pet deals more damage and doesn't run away.
Mend Pet (12) between fights keeps your pet ready, so you rarely stop.

levels.title: The pet tanks
tips: Aspect of the Cheetah (20) for travel. Swap back to Hawk before you pull.
Freezing Trap (20) holds an extra mob while you and the pet kill the first one.
Rapid Fire (26) is a big burst. Use it on hard mobs or when two attack you.
Keep your pet close to your level. Tame a new one if it falls behind.

levels.title: Feign and stun
tips: Feign Death (30) drops all threat. Use it when a pull goes wrong, then send the pet again.
Intimidation (33) stuns the mob. Save it for runners or an extra add.
Spirit Bond heals you and the pet slowly, so you rest even less.

levels.title: Bestial Wrath
tips: Bestial Wrath (40) sends your pet into a rage for 18 sec. Use it on every tough mob.
Most players get their first mount around 40. Save gold for it.
From 41, talents go to Marksmanship: Lethal Attacks for crit, Efficiency for mana.

levels.title: Fast finish
tips: Careful Aim turns Intellect into attack power. Mail with Agility and Intellect is ideal.
Train every new rank of your shots and Mend Pet; the pet needs it as much as you.
Rapid Killing boosts your next shot after each kill. Chain pulls to keep it going.

notes.4: Serpent Sting: open every fight with it.
notes.6: Arcane Shot and Hunter's Mark at the trainer.
notes.10: Taming quests at your class trainer. Your pet is your tank from now on.
notes.12: Mend Pet and Wing Clip at the trainer.
notes.16: Mongoose Bite: use it in melee after you dodge.
notes.20: Aspect of the Cheetah and Freezing Trap.
notes.33: Intimidation talent: your pet stuns the target.
notes.40: Bestial Wrath talent and Volley at the trainer.

end.title: Marksman raider
end.text: Trueshot Aura, Mortal Shots and Sniper Shot for steady ranged raid damage. Beast Mastery points keep the pet useful.

Mage.intro: The Mage is a ranged caster with huge burst and the best crowd control in the game. You conjure your own food and water, so you never pay for drinks. Frost is the safe way to level: your spells slow and freeze mobs, so they rarely reach you. Keep your distance and you will rarely die.
good: Free conjured food and water, no vendor trips
Slows and freezes keep mobs away from you
Strong AoE pulls with Frost Nova and Cone of Cold
Teleports to cities and portals to sell
bad: Very low health and armor
A bad pull can kill you in seconds

levels.title: Bolts and free drinks
tips: Keep Frost Armor and Arcane Intellect up at all times.
Learn Conjure Water at 4 and Conjure Food at 6. Make a stack before you leave town.
Open with Frostbolt: the slow gives you time for a second cast before the mob arrives.
Visit the trainer every even level. New ranks hit much harder.

levels.title: Freeze, step back, repeat
tips: When a mob reaches you, cast Frost Nova, walk away a few steps and keep casting.
Frostbite sometimes freezes the target for free. Use that time to cast again.
If a second mob joins, Polymorph it and finish the first one.
Buy a wand and use it to finish mobs when your mana is low.

levels.title: Ice Lance and Shatter
tips: Ice Lance does triple damage on frozen targets. Frost Nova, then two Ice Lances.
Shatter makes nearly every spell crit on frozen mobs. Freeze first, then blast.
Blink gets you out of melee range. Mana Shield soaks hits when a pull goes bad.
Use Evocation when you are out of mana instead of sitting to drink.

levels.title: Small AoE pulls
tips: Swap Frost Armor for Ice Armor at 30. Use Mage Armor if you drink too often.
Pull 2–3 mobs, Frost Nova them, step back and use Cone of Cold.
Cold Snap resets Frost Nova and Cone of Cold for a second round.
Keep a mana gem in your bags. It is free mana in a tight fight.

levels.title: Ice Barrier saves you
tips: Cast Ice Barrier before every pull. It absorbs damage and stops spell pushback.
Ice Block is your emergency button. Wait inside it for cooldowns, then run.
Portals arrive at 40. Other players will pay for a ride to the capital.

levels.title: Finish strong
tips: Winter's Chill: two Frostbolts first make your next Cone of Cold hit harder.
Do dungeons for gear with Intellect and Spell Damage.
Make water for your group. Healers will love you.

notes.4: Conjure Water: you will never buy a drink again.
notes.8: Polymorph turns an extra mob into a sheep. Your best tool vs. adds.
notes.10: Frost Nova and your first talent point (Improved Frostbolt).
notes.16: Flamestrike for groups, but it costs a lot of mana.
notes.20: Big level: Blink, Evocation, Mana Shield and city teleports.
notes.23: Ice Lance talent. Use it on frozen mobs only.
notes.26: Cone of Cold: AoE damage and slow in front of you.
notes.28: Conjure Mana Agate: an instant mana potion you make yourself.
notes.34: Mage Armor: lets your mana regen keep going while you cast.
notes.38: Ice Block talent. Learn to use it before you need it.
notes.40: Ice Barrier talent and portals to the capitals.
notes.58: Conjure Mana Ruby, your biggest mana gem.

end.title: Fire for raids
end.text: At 60, Fire turns crits into burning Ignite damage and long Combustion bursts. With Arcane for cheap Clearcasting spells and mana regen while casting, it is a strong raid damage spec.

Paladin.intro: A holy knight in plate who heals and protects himself. You keep a Seal active, judge it on the enemy and swing a big weapon. Kills are a bit slower than other classes, but you almost never die and rarely need to rest. At 60 groups want you as a healer.
good: Very hard to kill: plate, heals and shields
Little downtime thanks to self-heals
Welcome in every group as a healer or buffer
bad: Kills a bit slower than most classes
Mana runs low on long chains of fights
Few buttons, so it can feel repetitive

levels.title: Seal and judge
tips: Keep a Seal active. At 4, learn Judgement: it hits the mob with your Seal and the Seal stays.
Heal yourself with Holy Light after a fight instead of eating every time.
Wear the heaviest armor you can and use the biggest weapon you find.

levels.title: Blessings and auras
tips: Keep Blessing of Might and an aura up at all times. Recast the blessing when it fades.
Hammer of Justice stuns a mob for 3 sec: use it on runners or to stop a heal.
Lay on Hands (10) is a full heal on a long cooldown. It turns a death into a win.
Low health? Divine Protection, then heal. You can't attack while it lasts.

levels.title: Seal of Command
tips: Seal of Command comes from talents at 20. It loves a slow two-handed weapon.
Exorcism (20) only hits undead and demons, but hits hard. Undead zones are great for you.
Flash of Light (20) is a cheap, quick heal. Top up between pulls.
Pursuit of Justice makes you run faster, so less time walking between quests.

levels.title: Stun, then judge
tips: Stun with Hammer of Justice, then use Judgement with Seal of Command: it deals double damage.
Consecration (30) hurts every mob around you. Good for two or three, but costly on mana.
Divine Shield (34) makes you immune for a short time. Bubble, heal up, then fight on.
Champion of the Light turns your Intellect into Holy damage. Don't skip Intellect gear.

levels.title: Tougher and faster
tips: Most players get their first mount around 40. Save gold for it.
Low on mana? Fight with Seal of Wisdom for a while: hits give mana back.
Hammer of Wrath (44) finishes mobs under 20% health from range.
Templar's Bulwark at 50 gives a shield as big as your health. Use it on hard fights.

levels.title: Strong to the end
tips: Divine Strength and Improved Seals raise your damage for the last ten levels.
Keep training new ranks of Seal of Command, Consecration and your heals.
Greater blessings (52+) are for groups. Solo, the normal ones are enough.

notes.4: Judgement at the trainer. Seal, judge, swing: that's your fight.
notes.10: Lay on Hands: a full heal for emergencies.
notes.12: Redemption is learned through a class quest. Worth it for groups.
notes.16: Retribution Aura: extra damage when mobs hit you.
notes.20: Seal of Command talent. Get a slow two-handed weapon.
notes.44: Hammer of Wrath: ranged finisher under 20% health.
notes.50: Templar's Bulwark talent: a shield as big as your health.

end.title: Holy healer
end.text: Raids and dungeons want paladin healers. Illumination and Holy Shock keep mana up, Prot adds Intellect and a safety shield.

Priest.intro: A caster who can heal and deal Shadow damage. This guide levels you as Shadow: damage over time, Mind Blast, Mind Flay and later Shadowform. Spirit Tap and a wand keep your mana up, so you rest less. A shield and your own heals mean you rarely die.
good: Shield and heals make you hard to kill
Spirit Tap: very little drinking
Groups always want a priest healer
Psychic Scream gets you out of bad pulls
bad: Slow start until Mind Flay at 20
Cloth armor: melee mobs hurt
Needs a wand to save mana

levels.title: Smite and a wand
tips: Pull with Shadow Word: Pain, then Smite. Once you have a wand, finish mobs with it.
Look for a wand from quests, or buy one made by a Tailor or Enchanter. It saves a lot of mana.
Power Word: Shield (6) soaks damage. Cast it before the mob reaches you.
Drink between fights. Buy the best water the innkeeper sells.

levels.title: Spirit Tap
tips: Spirit Tap first: after each kill your mana returns fast. Pull the next mob right away.
Open with Mind Blast, add Shadow Word: Pain, then wand the mob down. Shield if it hits you.
Inner Fire (12) adds armor. Keep it and Power Word: Fortitude up all the time.
At 10 and 20, check your trainer: some priest spells depend on your race.

levels.title: Mind Flay
tips: Mind Flay (talent at 20) slows the mob and hits hard. Channel it while your shield holds.
Flash Heal (20) is your fast emergency heal. Renew is cheaper if you have time.
Two mobs on you? Psychic Scream, then kill one while the other runs away.
Vampiric Embrace (28) heals you for part of your Shadow damage.

levels.title: Shadow grows
tips: Pull from max range with Mind Blast. Shadow Reach gives extra range.
Shadow Weaving stacks with every Shadow spell, so each cast hits a bit harder.
While the shield absorbs hits, your casts are not slowed down. Keep it up.
Learn every new rank of Mind Blast, Mind Flay and Shadow Word: Pain.

levels.title: Shadowform
tips: Shadowform (40): more Shadow damage, half mana cost, less physical damage taken. Stay in it.
You can't heal in Shadowform. Leave it, heal, then go back in. The shield still works.
Twin Disciplines boosts instant spells like Shadow Word: Pain and the shield.
Save gold for riding at 40.

levels.title: Mana machine
tips: Pull two mobs: Shadow Word: Pain on both, then Mind Flay them one by one.
Meditation and Spirit Tap keep mana coming while you cast. You should rarely drink now.
Inner Focus (60) makes one spell free. Use it on a big Mind Blast.
Run dungeons for spell gear. Groups love a priest who can heal.

notes.4: Shadow Word: Pain: open every fight with it.
notes.6: Power Word: Shield: cast it before the mob reaches you.
notes.10: Spirit Tap first. Also check your trainer for a race spell.
notes.12: Inner Fire: extra armor. Keep it up.
notes.14: Psychic Scream: nearby mobs flee. Your panic button.
notes.20: Mind Flay, Flash Heal and Holy Fire. Big level!
notes.25: Shadow Weaving: each Shadow spell makes the next hit harder.
notes.28: Vampiric Embrace: your Shadow damage heals you.
notes.35: Darkness: more Shadow damage with every point.
notes.40: Shadowform! Stay in it except to heal.
notes.42: Twin Disciplines: instant spells hit harder.
notes.60: Inner Focus: one free spell with extra crit.

end.title: Holy raid healer
end.text: Faster, bigger heals and Prayer of Mending, with Discipline points for Intellect and mana regen. This is what raids and dungeons want most from a priest.

Rogue.intro: A sneaky melee fighter. You build combo points with attacks, then spend them on a finisher. This guide levels you as Combat with swords: cheap attacks, steady damage and big cooldowns. Energy refills fast and you use no mana, so your only downtime is eating after a fight.
good: High melee damage from level 1
Stealth lets you skip mobs and pick your fights
No mana: just eat to heal up
Great escapes: Sprint, Evasion, Vanish
bad: You eat after most fights
Weak when three mobs attack at once
Only Throw for a ranged pull

levels.title: Learn combo points
tips: Sinister Strike builds combo points. Spend them on Eviscerate at 3 to 5 points.
Sneak up in Stealth, or pull with Throw so the mob runs to you.
Eat after fights. Keep a stack of the best food the innkeeper sells.
Visit the trainer every even level: new ranks add a lot of damage.

levels.title: Slice and Dice
tips: Combat talents first: cheaper Sinister Strike and a stronger Eviscerate.
Open with a short Slice and Dice (1–2 points). Faster swings mean faster kills.
Hold two one-handers. Put the slow, hard-hitting one in your main hand.
Kick stops a caster's spell. Save Evasion for a fight that goes wrong.

levels.title: Poisons and stuns
tips: At 20 you can learn Poisons. Ask your rogue trainer, then coat your weapons for free extra damage.
Cheap Shot (26) opens from Stealth with a stun and 2 combo points.
Vanish (22) is your escape button. Get out, eat, try again.
You win 1 vs 1 easily. Look around for wandering mobs before you open.

levels.title: Blade Flurry
tips: Kidney Shot (30) stuns with your combo points. Use it when a fight turns bad.
Blade Flurry (36) hits a second mob too. Now pulling two at once pays off.
Hack and Slash loves swords: random extra attacks. Use a sword in each hand if you can.
Save gold for riding at 40.

levels.title: Adrenaline Rush
tips: Adrenaline Rush doubles your energy for 15 sec. Pair it with Blade Flurry on two mobs.
Now Assassination: Malice gives more crit on every attack.
Keep poisons on both weapons and carry spares. They run out mid-fight.
Low on health? Gouge the mob and bandage. First Aid is great for rogues.

levels.title: Finish strong
tips: Cold Blood (56) makes your next Eviscerate a sure crit. Use it to end a tough mob.
Improved Poisons makes poisons land far more often.
Two humanoids? Sap one, kill the other, then fight the second one fresh.
Run dungeons for weapons. Better weapons matter more than anything else.

notes.4: Backstab needs a dagger and you behind the mob. With swords, skip it.
notes.8: Evasion: press it when a mob hits hard or two mobs attack you.
notes.10: First talent point. Sap puts a humanoid to sleep before the fight.
notes.14: Garrote: a bleed opener from Stealth. Works with any weapon.
notes.20: Poisons and Rupture. Rupture is good on mobs with lots of health.
notes.22: Vanish: your way out when a pull goes wrong.
notes.25: Aggression: Sinister Strike and Eviscerate hit 15% harder.
notes.30: Kidney Shot: a finisher that stuns.
notes.31: Hack and Slash: swords get extra attacks, daggers get crit.
notes.36: Blade Flurry: start pulling two mobs on purpose.
notes.40: Adrenaline Rush and riding. Big level!
notes.41: Start Assassination with Malice for more crit.
notes.56: Cold Blood: a crit whenever you need one.

end.title: Mutilate daggers for raids
end.text: Swap to daggers and build combo points with Mutilate. Poison talents and Seal Fate make this a strong damage build for raids and dungeons.

Shaman.intro: A mix of melee, spells and totems. This guide levels you as Enhancement with a two-handed weapon: weapon buffs, Stormstrike and shocks. Your Intellect also adds attack power, so you hit hard and still have mana to heal. Drop a totem or two to make each fight easier.
good: Strong melee with a two-hander
Heals yourself between fights
Totems help in every fight
Reincarnation: revive yourself at 30
bad: Many buttons and totems to learn
Mana runs dry in long fights
Totems cost mana: don't spam them

levels.title: Bolt and shock
tips: Pull with Lightning Bolt, then melee. Earth Shock (4) is instant damage and stops a cast.
Keep Rockbiter Weapon on your weapon and Lightning Shield (8) on yourself.
At 4, your trainer has the Earth totem quest. It gives Stoneskin Totem.
Heal with Healing Wave after a fight, then drink if mana is low.

levels.title: Fire and totems
tips: At 10, do the Fire totem quest for Searing Totem. Drop it just before you pull.
Use a slow two-handed mace, axe or staff with Flametongue Weapon on it.
Flame Shock burns over time; Earth Shock stops casters. They share a cooldown.
Talents: more crit, and Mental Dexterity turns your Intellect into attack power.

levels.title: Ghost Wolf and Stormstrike
tips: Ghost Wolf (20) makes you run faster. At 20, also do the Water totem quest for Healing Stream Totem.
Stormstrike (25) hits now and boosts your next shock. Stormstrike, then Earth Shock.
Strength of Earth Totem adds Strength. Use it with Searing Totem on tough mobs.
Lesser Healing Wave (20) is a fast heal for emergencies.

levels.title: Windfury
tips: Windfury Weapon (30) gives random extra attacks. Huge on a slow two-hander.
Reincarnation (30) lets you revive yourself. Buy its reagent from a vendor.
Maelstrom Weapon: melee hits make your next Lightning Bolt faster and cheaper. Cast it at full stacks.
Mana Spring Totem (26) helps in long fights and while you rest.

levels.title: Rage of the Farseer
tips: Rage of the Farseer (40): 30% faster attacks for 25 sec. Use it on hard mobs.
Improved Ghost Wolf makes the cast almost instant. Use Ghost Wolf all the time.
Chain Heal (40) is for groups. Solo, Healing Wave or Lesser Healing Wave is enough.
Save gold for riding at 40.

levels.title: Totem master
tips: Toughness and Anticipation make you sturdy. With full mana, pull two mobs at once.
Convection makes shocks cheaper, so shock on every cooldown.
Earthbind Totem or Frost Shock stops mobs that run away.
Do dungeons: shamans heal well and groups want them.

notes.8: Lightning Shield: keep it up while you fight.
notes.10: Fire totem quest for Searing Totem. First talent point.
notes.15: Mental Dexterity: Intellect now gives attack power.
notes.20: Ghost Wolf and the Water totem quest.
notes.26: Flurry: faster swings after a crit.
notes.30: Windfury Weapon and Reincarnation. Big level!
notes.35: Maelstrom Weapon: melee hits speed up Lightning Bolt.
notes.40: Rage of the Farseer and Chain Heal.
notes.41: Improved Ghost Wolf: almost instant cast.

end.title: Restoration healer
end.text: Chain Heal, Riptide and Mana Tide Totem make you a top group healer. The Enhancement points add Intellect and crit. This is the role raids want most from a shaman.

Warlock.intro: The Warlock curses enemies with damage over time and lets a demon pet do the tanking. Affliction is a relaxed way to level: put your curses on the mob, let the Voidwalker hold it and drain its life to heal yourself. You trade health for mana with Life Tap, so you rarely sit down to rest.
good: A demon pet tanks for you from level 10
Drain Life heals you while it does damage
Life Tap means almost no resting for mana
Fear and Death Coil get you out of trouble
bad: Soul Shards fill your bags
Slow kills on a single mob early on
Weak without your pet

levels.title: Imp and first curses
tips: Your first demon, the Imp, comes from an early class quest. Keep it out at all times.
Put your damage over time spells up first, then finish with Shadow Bolt.
Life Tap turns health into mana. Eat food afterwards: health comes back cheaper.
At level 10, ask your trainer for the Voidwalker quest.

levels.title: Voidwalker tanks for you
tips: Send the Voidwalker in first and wait a second, so the mob stays on it.
Improved Corruption makes Corruption instant. Cast it on every mob.
Use Drain Soul when the mob is almost dead to get a Soul Shard.
Drain Life heals you. Use it instead of eating whenever a mob is still alive.

levels.title: Drain tanking
tips: Cast Demon Armor at 20. It gives much more armor than Demon Skin.
Nightfall can make your next Shadow Bolt instant. Use it right away.
Fel Concentration keeps Drain Life going even when you are hit.
Do the Succubus quest at 20, but keep the Voidwalker for solo play.

levels.title: Three curses and a drain
tips: Siphon Life, Corruption and Bane of Agony together boost Drain Life via Soul Siphon.
Get the Felhunter at 30 from its class quest. Good against casters.
Low on health and mana? Life Tap, then Drain Life on the next mob.
Two mobs: dot both, Fear one, drain the other.

levels.title: Wrack speeds it all up
tips: Wrack makes all your dots tick twice as fast. Cast it after they are up.
Death Coil heals you and scares the mob. Save it for emergencies.
Howl of Terror fears up to 5 mobs if a pull goes wrong.

levels.title: Tough and steady
tips: Molten Skin cuts all damage you take by 10%.
Inferno comes from a class quest around 50. A big stun for bad pulls.
Keep only a few Soul Shards. Destroy extra ones to save bag space.

notes.4: Corruption: your main damage spell for the whole game.
notes.6: Life Tap. Health is easy to get back, mana is not.
notes.8: Fear sends a mob running. Watch out, it can pull more mobs.
notes.10: Voidwalker quest and Drain Soul for Soul Shards.
notes.12: Health Funnel heals your pet with your own health.
notes.14: Drain Life: your best friend for the rest of the climb.
notes.18: Create Soulstone. Use it on yourself before risky pulls.
notes.25: Nightfall talent: watch for instant Shadow Bolt procs.
notes.30: Felhunter quest and the Siphon Life talent.
notes.40: Wrack talent and Howl of Terror.
notes.42: Death Coil: instant heal and a short fear.
notes.60: Bane of Doom: huge damage after one minute, for bosses.

end.title: Destruction for raids
end.text: At 60, Destruction gives big Shadow Bolt and Fire crits, and Conflagrate boosts your Shadow damage. Affliction points add hit and Shadow crit. A simple, strong raid damage spec.

Warrior.intro: A plate-wearing fighter who runs on rage. You build rage by hitting and being hit, then spend it on big strikes. Leveling is slow at first and gets much smoother once your two-handed weapon and Arms talents come together. At 60 you are a top tank or melee damage dealer.
good: Huge hits with a good two-handed weapon
Can tank dungeons and raids
One of the strongest classes at level 60
bad: Eat and rest after most fights early on
No self-heals, so a bad pull hurts
Very dependent on your weapon

levels.title: Charge in
tips: At 4, train Charge and Rend. Charge opens every fight and gives you rage to start with.
Rage comes from hitting and getting hit. Pull one mob at a time and eat between fights.
Swap to any better weapon you find. For a warrior, the weapon matters more than anything else.

levels.title: Stances and first talents
tips: At 10 your class trainer has a quest that teaches Defensive Stance and Sunder Armor. Do it.
Overpower lights up after a mob dodges. Press it right away: cheap and hard-hitting.
Improved Charge gives more rage at the pull, so you can open with Rend and a strike at once.
Use Hamstring on mobs that flee at low health so they don't bring friends.

levels.title: Rage that keeps flowing
tips: Anger Management at 20 gives rage over time. Bloodrage before a pull adds a head start.
Execute (24) finishes mobs under 20% health. Use it instead of Heroic Strike at the end.
Heroic Strike only with spare rage: it uses rage you may need for Overpower or Execute.
Near 30, look for warrior class quests. Some of them reward a strong two-handed weapon.

levels.title: Berserker and Slam
tips: At 30 your trainer starts the Berserker Stance quest. It also teaches Intercept.
Slam (30) has a short cast. After Improved Slam at 38 it no longer delays your swing.
Sweeping Strikes (32) plus Cleave makes two-mob pulls quick and safe.
Whirlwind comes from the trainer at 36. Great when several mobs are on you.

levels.title: Mortal Strike
tips: Mortal Strike (40) is your biggest hit. Press it every time it is ready.
With Bloodthrill, Rend makes Overpower show up much more often. Keep Rend on longer fights.
Pull went wrong? Retaliation or Intimidating Shout buys you time to win or run.
Spend the next points in Fury: Cruelty adds crit, which feeds Deep Wounds and Impale.

levels.title: The last push
tips: Recklessness (50) gives huge crits for a short time. Save it for elites or bad pulls.
Visit the trainer every two levels. Mortal Strike, Execute and Slam all get new ranks.
Run dungeons with a group when you can. One good two-hander speeds up everything.

notes.4: Charge and Rend at the trainer: this is your pull for the rest of the game.
notes.10: Class quest at your trainer: Defensive Stance and Sunder Armor.
notes.12: Overpower: use it every time a mob dodges.
notes.20: Anger Management talent: rage trickles in during every fight.
notes.24: Execute at the trainer. Finish every mob with it.
notes.30: Berserker Stance quest from your trainer, with Intercept as a bonus.
notes.32: Sweeping Strikes talent: pull two mobs and hit both.
notes.40: Mortal Strike talent. Most players get their first mount around now.
notes.48: Mortal Strike rank 2 at the trainer.

end.title: Fury dual-wield
end.text: Two one-handers, Flurry and Bloodthirst: the classic raid damage build. Arms points add rage and crit damage.
